reading: A correlation_ratio above 1.00 means the two legs landed together more often than independence predicts. Because a standard parlay is priced at the product of the legs, positively correlated legs make the parlay cheaper than it should be -- which is why some pairs show a positive return even though neither leg does on its own. That is a property of the pricing rule, not proof of skill, and it is why every pair is published rather than the best one.
method: Every unordered pair of strategies is combined whenever both fired in the same week in DIFFERENT games. The parlay price is the product of the two observed decimal prices. The whole matrix is published, so no pair is chosen after seeing the result.
pricing_note: The product of two legs is what a book would pay on a standard parlay. Because the legs are correlated, that price is only fair if the correlation is zero; the correlation_ratio column shows how far from zero it is.
